task.goal: A document importer extracts user-supplied ZIP files. It currently writes entries whose names contain ../ and may partially extract a good entry before discovering a bad one. Fix extract_archive(archive, destination) in archive.py: reject absolute paths, traversal and symbolic links before writing any file, preserve ordinary nested files, and return the extracted relative paths. Run visible tests and validate.

result.text:
I'll start by inspecting the workspace.Refreshing the stale visible-tests requirement after the later validation run.`extract_archive` in archive.py now validates every entry before any write: `_safe_name` rejects empty/absolute names (POSIX absolute, Windows drive or leading-separator forms), names whose parts contain `..` after normalizing both `/` and `\`, and entries whose Unix mode marks them as symlinks, raising `ValueError`. Member names are collected and validated in one pass first, then written, so a bad entry later in the archive leaves no partially extracted file. Ordinary nested entries are written under the destination and their relative names are returned in archive order.

Validation: `python3 -m unittest -v test_archive` passes (2 tests), and a scratch check confirmed rejection with zero filesystem writes for `/etc/evil.txt`, `C:\evil.txt`, `a/../../evil.txt`, `..\evil.txt`, and a symlink entry; a mixed archive with a valid large entry plus `../evil.txt` produced no output directory at all. Nested files `docs/readme.txt` and `docs/sub/a.bin` extracted correctly and were returned as `["docs/readme.txt", "docs/sub/a.bin"]`. Directory entries are still skipped; no changes were made to test_archive.py.
